prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: got to MIA airport early to check my bags and you're telling me I have to wait while you let other people check their bags.
Delta: Please accept our apology for the unfavorable impression you received in this instance. We appreciate your selection of Delta and... 1/2

Customer: has an issue with baggage disappearing at #CDG.  Do not check bags to Paris.
Delta: Oh no, Michael! Please file a claim with our Baggage Office in Paris so we can start the search for your bag.  *HDG

Customer: Oh , why book delta one when my bags come off last? I guess you prioritize the people who gate check their bags. For free.
Delta: ...Baggage Team at the airport regarding your bags?  *HCA 2/2

Customer: you don’t valet check bags for FC passengers when overheads are full? Has not been my experience with AA/UA...
Delta: Hi David, that would be cool. Regretfully we don't have that option. Please see a crew member for further assistance. *HPL

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: service_complaint):
"""I just spent 3 days in NYC freezing my butt off to avoid checking bags. On way home, had to check bags anyway. Adds 45 mins at ATL"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: We’re sorry for the inconvenience, especially after your chilly NYC trip. Please DM us with your itinerary so we can look into the bag‑check delay at ATL.
